How much does a motorcycle major service cost?

The big scheduled service — valves, fluids, plugs — what it costs, and what moves the price:

$650–$950

Valve check alone $650–$850 · minor service $475 · due every 15k–25k miles

Bay Area: no published metro-specific figure found — the national range is the honest reference.

Why quotes run $475 to $950+

Valve access
The adjustment itself is shims and gaskets — the money is teardown. Fairings, tank, and airbox off: 2 hours on a naked bike, 5–6 on a faired sportbike.
What's included
A real major service: valves, oil and filter, plugs, coolant flush, brake fluid flush, chain service. $650–$950 all-in at an independent shop.
Dealer vs. independent
Dealers bill more per hour and rarely less than book rate. A good independent does the same checklist for meaningfully less.
Plugs and extras
Plug labor alone is often $150+ on faired bikes — they're already in there for the valves, so don't pay teardown twice.

What the extra money buys

Minor service
~$475

Oil, filter, chain, fluids check, general inspection. The regular health check — do it on schedule and the major stays boring.

Major + valves
$650–$950

Everything in minor plus valve clearance check and adjustment, plugs, and coolant and brake fluid flushes. Due every 15,000–25,000 miles.

Bottom line: the major service is mostly labor for access — once the bike is apart, having everything done beats paying teardown twice.

Common questions

How often is a major service due?

Every 15,000–25,000 miles depending on the bike — the manual's number wins. Valves are the pacemaker; everything else hangs off that interval.

What happens if I skip the valve adjustment?

Tight valves burn; loose valves clatter and lose power. Worst case is a valve train rebuild at $3,000–$5,000 — the service is cheap insurance.

Can I do it myself?

If you can measure clearances and swap shims without rushing, yes — it's methodical, not magical. One mistake costs an engine, so be honest about your patience.

Why is it so much more than a car service?

Access. A car's valves sit under one cover; a sportbike's hide under fairings, tank, airbox, and frame spars. You're paying for disassembly.

Every bike prices differently.

The range above is published shop pricing. Your price depends on the bike and how buried the valves are. Take a photo of your bike in Brightglow for an estimate on the actual machine, and to compare local shops who've done the same work.
